item.title: Zipper: hiding bus latency for accelerators
item.description: A protocol layer that overlaps bus requests and exploits locality, so latency-sensitive accelerators keep running instead of waiting on the bus.

item.title: Twine: one interface for heterogeneous hardware
item.description: A Chisel extension that standardizes component interfaces and generates the control logic, so designers compose systems instead of wiring them.

item.title: Overpass: interconnect bandwidth for diverse components
item.description: A flexible interconnect with distributed resource allocation, so CPUs, accelerators, and I/O share bandwidth without one central arbiter.

item.title: Formally verifying a low-trust architecture
item.description: A complete formal verification of the Sequestered Encryption architecture, from the ISA down to RTL. CCS 2023 Distinguished Paper Award.

item.title: Morpheus: a moving target for attackers
item.description: A RISC-V secure architecture that keeps re-randomizing code and pointers underneath the running program, so attack probes go stale before they can be used.

item.title: How AI Changed the Way I Build
item.description: A frustrating document review led me, a computer architect with no web development experience, to build a tool with AI. As a personal project grew into a shared asset, it changed how I think about problems, products, and the workflows around them.

item.title: Within Myself
item.description: A second Ironman taught me more about my abilities, my fears, and my own rhythm. More rewarding than the finish was the life I built while preparing for it—and the confidence that I could keep it going.

item.title: Experience
item.description:
Work Experience

Tenstorrent Inc.

Santa Clara, CA · May 2022 – Present

Staff Architect · Oct 2026 – Present

  • Lead the in-house coherent fabric (CHI): transport, chip-to-chip links, and generators.
  • Fabric lead for a RISC-V CPU chiplet SoC: integrate CPU clusters, the coherent fabric, IOMMU, timers, and an AI compute engine; firmware runs end to end in simulation.
  • Lead AI-assisted hardware design: executable specs that generate golden models, RTL, and formal checks.
  • Set performance-modeling direction across the AI NoC and the coherent CPU fabric.
  • Mentor architects and interns; align modeling, RTL, and verification teams.

Senior Architect · May 2025 – Oct 2026

  • Chiplet NoC specs: owned non-coherent NoC specs for IO and LPDDR chiplets (topology, address maps, interleaving, KPIs, LPDDR controller width).
  • NoC RTL and debug: integrated trace, remap, and timeout features in an IO-chiplet fabric; fixed head-of-line blocking to meet bandwidth targets.
  • GDDR chiplet: drove bring-up, performance analysis, and debug: bandwidth correlation, unaligned-access fixes, and telemetry and timeout checks.
  • Third-party IP: ran design reviews and evaluations of commercial NoC and memory IP; wrapped vendor models for in-house simulation.
  • Performance modeling: CPU multicore scaling and SLC policies, AI-accelerator models correlated with RTL, and a cycle-accurate NoC simulator.
  • Fabric generators: built an AXI fabric generator adopted by SoC teams, and the in-house CHI fabric’s generator and formal environment.
  • Spec platform: built the internal service that builds, hosts, and reviews architecture specs (live editing, comments, AI review); teams use it for chip spec sign-off.
  • RISC-V ACLINT: generated RTL from an executable spec and checked it formally against the golden model.
  • Hiring and outreach: built interview frameworks, interviewed candidates, and supported university research collaborations.

Platform Architecture Intern · May 2023 – Aug 2023

  • Studied multi-core, multi-chiplet fabric changes for performance and power; estimated on- and off-chip traffic for power planning.
  • Defined cache and fabric verification testplans and built traffic-generation and simulation workflows.

Platform Architecture Intern · May 2022 – Aug 2022

  • Contributed to architecture studies for a server-class RISC-V multicore CPU.
  • Built a configurable fabric performance model for heterogeneous multicore systems.

Education

PhD in Computer Science and Engineering

University of Michigan, Ann Arbor, MI · 2019 – 2025

item.title: General Purpose FTW
item.description: You can’t guess the next model, computing was never only matmul, and the expensive parts have to stay busy. Computing has never concentrated on one workload — the thing that needs justifying isn’t generality, it’s specialization.

item.title: Verification Is an Architect's Love Language
item.description: Two years ago I turned down verification without a second thought. Now it’s one of the things I talk about most. AI can explore a design space — but only once someone has drawn the boundary, and verification is the only executable way an architect gets design intent across.

item.title: Overcoming Fear: What Open Water Swimming Taught Me
item.description: Of the three legs of a triathlon, swimming is the one that scares me most. Notes on why open water breaks down control, and what building competence, staying present, and accepting the worst case actually do to fear.

item.title: It's Not Rocket Science: Designing an AI Computer That Scales
item.description: The hardest part of chip architecture was never mastering some arcane secret — it’s deciding what to do and what not to do under real constraints. The question is how to design a computer that can actually be used at scale, not a machine that only works with the most advanced process node, the deepest pockets, and the most specialized team.

item.title: Hooding and Notes from Work
item.description: Parents in town for hooding and travel—notes from my first real break after work on why shipping silicon is largely a management problem, slow feedback loops in hardware, the mindset behind heavy AI use, and why we need a better AI computer, not a faster niche accelerator.

item.title: April Fools, Fitness Coaching, and Two Real Questions
item.description: An April Fools prank sparked two genuine questions — am I pursuing what makes me happy, and has AI actually made humanity happier?

item.title: The Motorcycle and the Zen: Reading Notes
item.description: Care is on the human side, Quality is on the object side, and engagement is the thread connecting them. Reading notes on Zen and the Art of Motorcycle Maintenance.

item.title: ARM, RISC-V, and AI
item.description: Three questions on the ARM vs. RISC-V battle — what RISC-V actually has going for it in the AI era, why ARM is now making its own SoC, and where RISC-V still has ground to cover.

item.title: Why I Always Show Up at the Office
item.description: It is not just about separating work from life — it is about not missing the serendipitous collisions that only happen in person.

item.title: Computer Architecture Is Entering a Golden Era
item.description: AI-native workloads, edge fragmentation, and faster experimentation are pushing architecture back to the center of hardware value creation.

item.title: Semiconductor Development Cycles Will Shrink Faster Than Expected
item.description: As prototyping, validation, and silicon feedback loops shrink from months to days, chip development will start to move at a cadence much closer to software.

item.title: Using AI Well Starts with Redesigning the Workflow
item.description: Getting real leverage from AI requires more than adding a model to existing processes. It requires rethinking workflow design, sign-off cost, and the role of infrastructure.

item.title: Saying No Is a Commitment to Your Long-Term Goals
item.description: Setting boundaries and saying no is not cold-hearted; it is how you protect focus for what matters most.

item.title: From Book Smart and Street Smart to System Smart
item.description: For complex projects, isolated skills are not enough; scalable systems set the ceiling.

item.title: Streamlining High-Performance Heterogeneous Hardware Design
item.description: PhD dissertation. Twine, Zipper, and Overpass address the communication bottlenecks of heterogeneous hardware: mismatched interfaces, poor latency tolerance, and contended interconnect bandwidth.

item.title: Zipper: Latency-Tolerant Optimizations for High-Performance Buses
item.description: Zipper is a protocol optimization layer that reduces bus communication latency by enabling device and request level parallelism and exploiting data locality — achieving 8x speedup with under 5% logic overhead.

item.title: Security Verification of Low-Trust Architectures
item.description: A complete formal verification of the Sequestered Encryption (SE) low-trust architecture, proving security against direct data disclosures and digital side channels for all possible programs, demonstrated across seven correct and buggy RTL implementations.

item.title: Twine: A Chisel Extension for Component-Level Heterogeneous Design
item.description: Twine is a Chisel extension that standardizes hardware component interfaces and supports control-free specification with flexible data type conversion, considerably improving reusability for heterogeneous designs.

item.title: Morpheus: A Vulnerability-Tolerant Secure Architecture Based on Ensembles of Moving Target Defenses with Churn
item.description: Morpheus is a RISC-V secure architecture that combines ensembles of moving target defenses with churn to continuously re-randomize pointers and code, achieving high-coverage protection against control-flow attacks with negligible (1%) performance overhead.

item.title: CommPact: Evaluating the Feasibility of Autonomous Vehicle Contracts
item.description: CommPact proposes Autonomous Vehicle contracts using Intel SGX secure enclaves to enforce agreed-upon driving rules in platoons, allowing safe contract termination within 1.5 seconds of an attack.
